reviews.reasoning: Re-derived from the toolkit rather than from the row. The row's single Hebrew quote נְאֻֽם collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.36.2 = web:Ps.36.1, so it is quotation-grade; its skeleton sweep returns 2 verses book-wide (oshb:Ps.36.2 = web:Ps.36.1 and oshb:Ps.110.1 = web:Ps.110.1), which means the oracular-usage gloss rests on one in-book parallel and carries no digit in the row - an observation I note rather than file. THE SEAM ITSELF I DO NOT CONTEST, and I re-derived it independently instead of trusting the row: a pointed kaf-final scan over oshb:Ps.36.1-Ps.36.5 = web:Ps.36.0-Ps.36.4 returns 0 second-person-masculine-singular suffix tokens across those 5 verses, while the next verse carries two, חַסְדֶּ֑ךָ and אֱ֝מֽוּנָתְךָ֗ at oshb:Ps.36.6 = web:Ps.36.5; WEB agrees, with 0 you/your tokens across web:Ps.36.0-Ps.36.4 (5 verses) against 2 in “Your loving kindness, Yahweh, is in the heavens. Your faithfulness reaches to the skies.” (web:Ps.36.5). The addressee pivot lands exactly where the row draws it, which is why high confidence on the boundary is defensible even with defective prose evidence. Disclosure obligations checked, none arise: the selah inventory records 0 entries in Ps 36 (span-scoped) and the ketiv/qere inventory 0 notes in Ps 36; the paseq inventory records segs at oshb:Ps.36.1 = web:Ps.36.0, oshb:Ps.36.5 = web:Ps.36.4 and oshb:Ps.36.7 = web:Ps.36.6 (seg layer, single-witness), which the row neither cites nor needs. The universals checker flags the rejected_alternative's addressee-change sentence; I tested it rather than repeating it - 0 tokens of second-person address in the 3 verses web:Ps.36.1-Ps.36.3, in both witnesses - so the claim is span-true and the flag is satisfiable. Also available and unused: the title at oshb:Ps.36.1 = web:Ps.36.0 is one of only 2 verses book-wide whose skeleton carries the servant-of-YHWH attribution (oshb:Ps.18.1 = web:Ps.18.0 and oshb:Ps.36.1 = web:Ps.36.0), a tier-1 opener signal the row cites in refs without arguing it. What fails is content: the row misplaces the heart in which the utterance sits, and its terminal-verse demonstration quotes the verse before the one it cites. Tier-0 clears both - the WEB quote checker returned 0 flags over 4 quotes because it grants one verse of slack on both sides of a cited edge - so both are model territory.

challenges.claim: The row locates the utterance in the wicked man's heart, but the Hebrew it cites carries a first-person-singular suffix, so the reading it glosses is not the text in either witness.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.36.2 = web:Ps.36.1 reads בְּקֶ֣רֶב לִבִּ֑י (collate tier: byte, quotation-grade) - the suffix is first-person-singular yod; the contrasting third-person-masculine-singular form in the same verse is עֵינָֽיו at its close. WEB renders the clause “A revelation is within my heart about the disobedience of the wicked” (web:Ps.36.1), the psalmist's heart - and that is the row's OWN quoted text, sitting in the same rationale sentence that calls it the wicked man's own heart; observed_substrate_signals[0] repeats it as applied ironically to the wicked man's own heart. A his-heart reading is attested in other traditions, but oshb:Ps.36.2 = web:Ps.36.1 is not one of the two recorded variant/rendering zones of this book, so nothing in the row discloses a departure from the staged bytes. Knock-on: the rationale asserts an unbroken third-person he/his run over web:Ps.36.1-Ps.36.4 = oshb:Ps.36.2-Ps.36.5, which the first-person suffix in the run's opening verse contradicts - the third-person material there is the wicked man as the OBJECT of an utterance received in the speaker's heart. Since observed_substrate_signals carries the same wording, the repair is one edit across both fields.

challenges.claim: The curly-quoted WEB clause offered as the span's terminal verse belongs to the preceding verse, so the rear-seam demonstration is bound to the wrong ref.
challenges.evidence: The rationale attaches “He has ceased to be wise and to do good.” to web:Ps.36.4 = oshb:Ps.36.5. That clause is web:Ps.36.3, which reads “The words of his mouth are iniquity and deceit. He has ceased to be wise and to do good.” (web:Ps.36.3). The verse actually cited reads “He plots iniquity on his bed. He sets himself in a way that is not good. He doesn’t abhor evil.” (web:Ps.36.4). Hebrew settles the offset independently of the English: חָדַ֖ל לְהַשְׂכִּ֣יל לְהֵיטִֽיב sits in oshb:Ps.36.4 = web:Ps.36.3 (collate tier: byte), while oshb:Ps.36.5 = web:Ps.36.4 opens אָ֤וֶן יַחְשֹׁ֗ב (collate tier: byte). The dual-cite arithmetic web:Ps.36.4 = oshb:Ps.36.5 is itself correct; it is the quote that is mis-seated. The Tier-0 WEB quote checker returns 0 flags on this row because it grants one verse of slack on both sides of a cited edge, so this passes machine check and still fails as evidence. The substantive point survives on the correct verse's own bytes - oshb:Ps.36.5 = web:Ps.36.4 carries three third-person-masculine-singular prefix-conjugation verbs, יַחְשֹׁ֗ב, יִ֭תְיַצֵּב and יִמְאָֽס - so the cure is a re-cut of quote and ref together, with the gloss re-cut to the same verse, not a warrant swap.

reviews.reasoning: Re-derived independently. All 5 dual pairs the row carries satisfy the shift+1 arithmetic, the span closes the psalm (12 WEB verses; the psalm's two rows tile web:Ps.36.1-Ps.36.12 with 0 gaps and 0 overlaps), and both curly-quoted WEB spans check verbatim at their cited refs (2 of 2). The front seam is sound on bytes I re-derived myself: the psalm's opening second-person forms (2 tokens) are חַסְדֶּ֑ךָ and אֱ֝מֽוּנָתְךָ֗ at oshb:Ps.36.6 = web:Ps.36.5, with 0 such tokens in the 5 preceding verses oshb:Ps.36.1-Ps.36.5 = web:Ps.36.0-Ps.36.4. Where the row breaks down is the rear of the span. Its observed_substrate_signal (1 of 1 entries) asserts that the second-person address runs to the close at web:Ps.36.12 = oshb:Ps.36.13, and that is false in both witnesses: the same scan puts 2ms suffixes in oshb:Ps.36.6-Ps.36.11 = web:Ps.36.5-Ps.36.10 (6 consecutive verses) and returns 0 in oshb:Ps.36.12 = web:Ps.36.11 and 0 in oshb:Ps.36.13 = web:Ps.36.12, with 0 you/your tokens in each of the 2 verses at the close. The span is still right - the psalm's final verse has to land in its final row, and rows do not cross psalm boundaries - but the warrant as written does not reach the verses it is asked to hold. Two further defects follow from the same under-reading of the close: the rival the rejected_alternative disposes of is one verse late, since the speech-act turn is the command at oshb:Ps.36.11 = web:Ps.36.10 rather than the petition at web:Ps.36.11 that continues it; and the vocabulary run is asserted as a blended triad when just 2 of its 3 members reach web:Ps.36.10. The medium confidence is the one well-calibrated thing here: the internal question at web:Ps.36.9|Ps.36.10 is genuinely open, and the row is right that lexical recurrence binds that verse back to the hymn - חַסְדֶּ֑ךָ at oshb:Ps.36.6 = web:Ps.36.5, חַסְדְּךָ֗ at oshb:Ps.36.8 = web:Ps.36.7, חַ֭סְדְּךָ at oshb:Ps.36.11 = web:Ps.36.10, 3 verses in this psalm by skeleton sweep - it simply never joins that argument to the rival actually on offer.

WEB agrees with a digit: 0 you/your tokens in “Don’t let the foot of pride come against me. Don’t let the hand of the wicked drive me away.” (web:Ps.36.11) and 0 in “There the workers of iniquity are fallen. They are thrust down, and shall not be able to rise.” (web:Ps.36.12), against 2-3 per verse across web:Ps.36.5-Ps.36.10 (6 verses). The last verse carrying second-person address is web:Ps.36.10 = oshb:Ps.36.11, two verses short of the close the signal names. I am not contesting the span; I contest the evidence offered for its rear extent - 1 of 1 substrate entries - which also propagates into the rationale's claim that the closing petition stays in the same second-person address.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative disposes of a rival split one verse later than the one the text offers: the turn from declarative hymn to petition opens at web:Ps.36.10, not at web:Ps.36.11.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.36.11 = web:Ps.36.10 opens on מְשֹׁ֣ךְ (collate tier: byte), which both witnesses read as a command rather than a statement - WEB renders the verse “Oh continue your loving kindness to those who know you, your righteousness to the upright in heart.” (web:Ps.36.10) - and it is the first non-declarative clause in the span, the 5 verses oshb:Ps.36.6-Ps.36.10 = web:Ps.36.5-Ps.36.9 being declarative throughout. The verse the row treats as the rival's start only continues that petition register: oshb:Ps.36.12 = web:Ps.36.11 is אַל תְּ֭בוֹאֵנִי רֶ֣גֶל גַּאֲוָ֑ה וְיַד רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים אַל תְּנִדֵֽנִי (collate tier: byte), a negative-particle petition pair, rendered “Don’t let the foot of pride come against me. Don’t let the hand of the wicked drive me away.” (web:Ps.36.11). The rival actually available is therefore a petition close of web:Ps.36.10-Ps.36.12 = oshb:Ps.36.11-Ps.36.13, while the row disposes of a 2-verse tail. This matters because the row's own driver is the discourse frame: by that same criterion a command cluster is a seam candidate, and the second-person-suffix evidence stops at the very verse in question (2ms tokens present at oshb:Ps.36.11 = web:Ps.36.10, 0 in each of the 2 verses after it). The row's lexical counter-argument is real - חַ֭סְדְּךָ and וְ֝צִדְקָֽתְךָ֗ at oshb:Ps.36.11 = web:Ps.36.10 recur from חַסְדֶּ֑ךָ at oshb:Ps.36.6 = web:Ps.36.5, חַסְדְּךָ֗ at oshb:Ps.36.8 = web:Ps.36.7 and צִדְקָֽתְךָ֨ at oshb:Ps.36.7 = web:Ps.36.6 - but it is aimed at the wrong seam. Form caveat stated plainly: the staged extract exposes no morphology layer, so the command reading is argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings, not from a machine tag.

challenges.claim: The rationale runs three lexical items together as one bundle said to reach web:Ps.36.10, but the faithfulness member occurs in 1 verse and stops at web:Ps.36.5.
challenges.evidence: Skeleton sweeps scoped to this psalm, unit = verses. Loving-kindness: 3 verses - חַסְדֶּ֑ךָ at oshb:Ps.36.6 = web:Ps.36.5, חַסְדְּךָ֗ at oshb:Ps.36.8 = web:Ps.36.7, חַ֭סְדְּךָ at oshb:Ps.36.11 = web:Ps.36.10. Righteousness: 2 verses - צִדְקָֽתְךָ֨ at oshb:Ps.36.7 = web:Ps.36.6 and וְ֝צִדְקָֽתְךָ֗ at oshb:Ps.36.11 = web:Ps.36.10. Faithfulness: 1 verse - אֱ֝מֽוּנָתְךָ֗ at oshb:Ps.36.6 = web:Ps.36.5, and nowhere after it in this psalm (0 further verses). All three splices collate at byte tier. The blended formulation therefore overstates: two of the three members reach web:Ps.36.10 = oshb:Ps.36.11, the third does not recur. Naming the swept object before its count, with the unit, repairs the sentence without weakening it, since the two members that do recur are the ones carrying the seam weight.
